title: What are access modifiers in C#?
description: Learn about public, private, protected, internal, and more.

data.text: **Question:** What are access modifiers in C#?
Access modifiers control the visibility and accessibility of classes, methods, and properties. C# provides public, private, protected, internal, protected internal, and private protected modifiers.

**Public:** Accessible from anywhere in the application.
**Private:** Accessible only within the containing class or struct.
**Protected:** Accessible within its class and by derived classes.
**Internal:** Accessible only within the same assembly (project).
**Protected Internal:** Accessible from the same assembly or from derived classes in other assemblies.
**Private Protected:** Accessible only within its class and derived classes in the same assembly.

data.title: Access Modifiers

data.caption: Access modifiers control visibility from anywhere in the app down to the containing class only.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Private: accessible only in containing class
Protected: accessible in class and derived classes
data.takeaway: Use the most restrictive modifier that still allows your code to work.
